review_notes:
I read the whole file. I did not open any related source files and based the review on the supplied text alone. The simp interface is small. It has two `@[simp]` lemmas: `toSimpleGraph_adj` and `numMarkings_of_isEmpty`.

- `toSimpleGraph_adj` rewrites `G.toSimpleGraph.Adj v w` to `v ≠ w ∧ G.Adj v w`. That is a sensible direction. `Adj` is an opaque `def`, so the right-hand side does not expand further, and I see no cycle.
- `numMarkings_of_isEmpty` rewrites to `0`, has generic instance arguments, and does not compete with other rules.
- The `_def` and `_iff` lemmas (`valence_def`, `numMarkings_def`, `firstBetti_def`, `arithmeticGenus_def`, `logCanonicalDegree_def`, `isStable_iff`, `isRationalTail_iff`, and similar) are deliberately not simp. They are definitional unfoldings. Making them simp would unfold the invariants everywhere and hide the graph-level lemmas, so I would not recommend that.
- `valence_eq_zero_iff` is not simp. Its only use is a single `simp [valence, filter_eq_empty_iff]` in its own proof, so tagging it would not help any use in this file.

I found no missing canonical simp lemma, wrong orientation, competing rules or cycle that I could support from the file. I did not look for uses outside this file, so there is some uncertainty about downstream files.
